Perilous

/PAIR-uh-luss/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Perilous means full of danger or risk; hazardous

Perilous means full of danger or risk. Early fur traders made a perilous crossing over the half-frozen river, testing each step as the ice groaned beneath them.

Worked Example

The window-washing crew worked the fiftieth-floor scaffold in gusting winds, re-clipping their harnesses one buckle at a time as the platform swayed beneath them.

Every detail, the extreme height, the gusting wind, the swaying platform, points to a serious risk of injury or death. A task surrounded by that much danger is perilous.

How Perilous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hazardous

hazardous: full of risk to health or safety

treacherous

treacherous: dangerous in a hidden or deceptive way

unsafe

unsafe: likely to cause harm or injury

Antonyms

safe

safe: free from danger or harm

secure

secure: protected against threat or loss

How Strong Is It? — risky → perilous → deadly

risky vs. perilous

risky vs. perilous: A risky choice carries some chance of harm, but a perilous one places you in serious, immediate danger.

deadly vs. perilous

deadly vs. perilous: A perilous route threatens your safety, but a deadly one has already proven that it kills.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — peril

Root — peril: danger (Latin periculum)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Peril ('danger,' from Latin periculum) plus -ous ('full of') builds 'full of danger,' which is the word's exact meaning.

Use the root in a new word: peril

Use the root in a new word: peril: The hikers understood the peril of setting out so close to dark.

Word Choice

Slightly formal / literary

Often paired with journeys and undertakings: 'a perilous journey,' 'a perilous crossing,' 'a perilous climb.' Perilous is about danger and risk, not about failure; a perilous plan might still succeed. Distinguish it from 'precarious,' which emphasizes instability and uncertainty rather than outright danger.
